content.title: About
content.content: Oysters are marine bivalve mollusks that live in coastal waters. Steaming preserves their natural briny flavor, tender texture, and most of their nutrients. They are often served hot, drizzled with sauce or lemon.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: An oyster can filter up to 50 liters of water per day, helping to clean its environment.
They have been considered a delicacy for more than 3,000 years, mentioned in ancient Chinese and Roman texts.
Oysters contain more zinc per serving than any other food.
They can change sex depending on environmental conditions.
In Japan, the tradition of “omakase” lets diners choose oysters without knowing the exact variety.

items.title: Rich in zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function, wound healing, and reproductive health.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Steamed oysters provide few calories while delivering protein and minerals.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s promote heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: The protein in oysters is easily digestible and supports muscle growth.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to oysters.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Oysters can accumulate toxins and bacteria, so purchase them from reputable sources.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: While modest, the cholesterol in oysters should be considered by those with high cholesterol.

items.title: Raw food safety
items.content: Steamed oysters may still harbor live microbes; ensure they are fully heated through.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve steamed oysters hot, often with lemon, soy sauce, or a butter‑based sauce. They can be eaten directly from the shell using a fork, or the meat can be removed and added to soups, pastas, or salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep live oysters in the refrigerator on a bed of damp cloth, no more than 2 days. Cooked oysters should be stored in an airtight container in the fridge and consumed within 24 hours.
